ufbx_write — vendored source
=============================

Upstream:  https://github.com/ufbx/ufbx-write
Commit:    2b65caaaa7fada7db9a2d25cd924997838169056
License:   MIT OR Unlicense — see LICENSE

What is vendored
----------------
An unmodified copy of `ufbx_write.h` and `ufbx_write.c`. Refreshing this
directory is a plain re-copy of a newer commit (update the hash above, then
re-run the workspace tests — in particular `crates/optimize`'s export
round-trip, which re-imports written files through the vendored ufbx reader).

Stability
---------
Upstream states plainly that ufbx_write "is still a work-in-progress, and
issues/breaking changes are to be expected". That is why the commit is pinned
rather than tracking a branch, and why the export round-trip test exists: a
breaking change upstream should fail a test here rather than silently produce
files that no longer load.

How it is built
---------------
`crates/optimize/build.rs` compiles this alongside `src/export_bridge.c` with
`cc`, and sets `cfg(has_ufbxw)` only when this directory is present — the same
optional-vendoring contract `crates/import` has for ufbx. Delete this directory
and the workspace still builds; export then reports `OptError::Unavailable`.

`ufbx_write.c` needs C99 or later. It has no OS-specific code and no threading
unless explicitly opted in, so nothing extra is configured. Note the header
defines `ufbxw_real` as `double`, so every coordinate crossing the bridge is
`f64` — `crates/optimize/src/export.rs` converts on the way in.
